learning_objectives.statement: Build and document a bounded ASP.NET Core expense API slice using the shared DTO contract, EF Core projection, validation, and safe error responses.
Record actual HTTP, database, async, logging, and authentication observations while distinguishing unavailable, deferred, and unverified work.

concepts.name: EF Core, validation, and safe failures

activity.title: Stage 05 ASP.NET Core API, EF Core, safety, and evidence
activity.instructions:
This bounded activity maps to DotNet-React-Roadmap/5.md and depends on the
Stage 04 schema/query/transaction work. It is a learner-attestation task,
not a claim that the full Stage 05 gate has passed.

Work only in a learner-owned scratch project and a separate learning database
named ExpenseApiDb. Do not use production data, real credentials, real
tokens, or a committed password/connection string. Keep secrets in local
development configuration or an environment/secret manager and record only
the configuration boundary, never its secret value. If the SDK, database,
migration tool, HTTP client, or test tooling is unavailable, record the
blocker and leave the relevant evidence incomplete.

1. Write the shared contract before implementation. CreateRequest must use
   categoryId, amount, spentOn, and optional note; ExpenseResponse must use
   id, categoryId, categoryName, amount, spentOn, and optional note. Record
   the exact JSON request and response observed from the learner's own run.
   Do not return the EF entity or rename categoryName to a nested category.
2. Design and implement a small API slice for GET /api/expenses,
   GET /api/expenses/{id}, and POST /api/expenses. If the learner adds PUT
   or DELETE, state their replacement/deletion semantics separately. Record
   actual method, route, status, response body, and empty/not-found behavior.
   Use 201 with a location when creation succeeds only if that is what the
   implementation actually returns; do not invent a status.
3. Keep the EF boundary observable: ExpenseApiDbContext, Category navigation,
   a migration against ExpenseApiDb, async database calls, and a projection
   to ExpenseResponse. Record the migration name, query/projection boundary,
   and any SQL/log observation actually seen. Do not claim that Include is
   always one query or that a DbContext is universally scoped. Defer a true
   optimistic-concurrency/rowversion proof to the later concurrency stage;
   a Stage05 409 may be documented only when an actual conflict contract is
   implemented and observed.
Record the actual service registration/lifetime decision and one inspected
projection/query observation. Check one AI claim against its concrete
conditions (lifetime, query count, JWT signing/encryption or blocking).
Cite the inspected configuration/code; a claim without evidence is incomplete.

4. Exercise validation with categoryId <= 0 or missing, a negative amount,
   an invalid/default date, a missing category, malformed binding, and an
   unknown id where applicable. Record the exact input, status, and safe
   response shape. Use ProblemDetails or ValidationProblemDetails only when
   the running API produces it; never paste a fabricated error.
5. Add async/cancellation boundaries and exception handling. Record the
   cancellation token boundary and a real failure response if exercised.
   Client responses must not expose stack traces, passwords, tokens,
   connection strings, or other secrets; record only safe server-log fields.
6. Add structured/searchable ILogger events and inspect a real request or
   failure log. Confirm that sensitive values are absent without copying
   secrets into the evidence note. Explain one correlation-id path if the
   implementation has one, or mark it as a gap.
7. Add authentication and authorization only after the CRUD slice is stable.
   Record the configured flow and actual 401/403/authorized observations,
   without treating a signed JWT as encrypted or putting secrets in a token.
   Keep signing keys outside source and explain HTTPS/storage/CSRF/XSS
   considerations that apply to the selected flow. If auth is not runnable,
   record the blocker rather than claiming protection.
8. Finish with a request-to-response checkpoint: middleware, endpoint or
   service, EF, database, and response. Attach the exact commands, status
   and response observations, migration/schema evidence, safe log excerpts,
   and a short list of incomplete or deferred items. All results must come
   from the learner's own scratch run; no expected output is a test result.

Stage 04 remains a prerequisite for relational schema, joins, grouping,
parameter safety, and transaction boundaries. The full Stage 05 project
remains broader than this guided activity and includes pagination/date
filtering, PUT/DELETE, migration work, ProblemDetails, logging, testing,
and authentication.
activity.expected_output: A learner evidence note with shared DTO JSON, actual endpoint/status/response observations, EF migration and projection evidence, validation and safe-error records, async/log/auth observations, a request-to-response checkpoint, and explicit blockers or deferred concurrency items.

rubric.evidence: The note shows the exact shared DTO fields and records learner-observed methods, routes, statuses, JSON responses, and not-found or empty behavior without fabricated results.
The note identifies the scratch ExpenseApiDbContext/migration/projection boundary and records actual validation or binding inputs and safe response shapes; unavailable tooling remains incomplete.

rubric.criterion: Error, logging, async, and auth safety
rubric.evidence: The note records observed async/error/log/auth behavior, excludes secrets and stack traces, distinguishes 401 from 403, and labels unrun or deferred concurrency work.
The note traces one request through middleware, endpoint/service, EF, database, and response, cites actual artifacts, and lists incomplete or deferred items instead of asserting completion.
